findings.rule: Policy must be in force at the incident date (on or after inception and on or before expiry); the incident must fall outside the 72-hour waiting period or the policy be a continuous renewal with no lapse over 14 days; the tier on the policy must cover the peril; the event must be a covered event.
findings.explanation: The incident date of 2026-05-04 falls between inception (2025-07-05) and expiry (2026-07-04), so the period-of-cover check in 2.4 is met. The incident occurred 303 days after inception, well outside the 72-hour waiting period in 2.5. The COMP tier covers own damage under 1.1, and a collision with a delivery van while the insured vehicle was being driven is a covered event under 2.1. The incident was in Australia and premium was paid, so cover was in force.

findings.rule: A claim must be notified within 30 calendar days of the incident date (clause 2.1); beyond 90 days requires decline unless a clause 2.3 exception is approved.
findings.explanation: The claim was notified 1 day after the incident, well within the 30-day window. No late-notification exception is needed.

findings.rule: No supplied exclusion applies: vehicle use matches declared use, no alcohol/drug reading, licence valid, registration current, driver is the policyholder, and no override was recorded.
findings.explanation: Vehicle was used privately, consistent with the declared use, so the absolute commercial/hire exclusion 3.7 is not triggered. Nothing in the facts points to alcohol, drug, licence, unlisted driver or registration issues, and no exclusion override or exception was recorded. The only supplied exclusions are 3.7, 3.13 (theft only, not relevant to a collision) and 3.18 (consequential loss, not claimed).

findings.rule: Tracks tested in order (SIU, Complex, Fast-track, Standard); first met is assigned. Triage within 1 business day of lodgement.
findings.explanation: SIU not met (score 0, no indicators). Complex not met (value 22,000 ≤ 50,000, no injury, liability clear, no total loss). Fast-track not met (value > 5,000 and third party involved). Standard is therefore correct. Triage occurred within 1 business day. No track boundary was crossed after triage (assessed 21,000 still within Standard).

findings.rule: Clause 4.2 requires the assessment to be completed within 10 business days of allocation. The supplied facts record no allocation date, so that timeframe cannot be measured. The closest figure is bd_triage_to_assessment (5), which is measured from triage and not from allocation. No supplied clause says how to measure from triage when allocation is unrecorded.
findings.calculation: Triage to assessment is 5 business days. This is within 3 + 10 = 13 business days, which is the maximum if allocation happened on the last permitted day. Allocation date is not recorded.
findings.explanation: A field assessment was required and done. Triage to assessment took 5 business days, so any allocation date inside the window would also meet the 3-day allocation and 10-day completion limits. The allocation date is missing, so the rule cannot be formally confirmed. The missing allocation date is flagged for review. Likely compliant.

findings.rule: Clause 4.4(b) requires a second assessment where the variance between claimed and assessed quantum exceeds the greater of 30% and AUD 20,000. Clause 4.5 requires the assessment to be no more than 90 calendar days old at the settlement decision. Clause 4.3 requires an independent external assessor for claims above AUD 100,000.
findings.calculation: Variance = 22000 - 21000 = 1000, which is 4.5% of 22000. Threshold is the greater of 30% (6600) and 20000, so 20000. 1000 is not above 20000. Assessment age is 33 days, within 90 days. The claim value of 22000 is not above 100000.
findings.explanation: A field assessment was done as required by 4.1. No second assessment is triggered, because the variance is below the threshold and there is no recorded written dispute or conflict of interest. The assessment was fresh at decision. The independent assessor threshold does not apply.

findings.rule: Approver must hold settlement authority covering the total incurred cost of the claim; single payment, no exception, no total loss, no litigation or catastrophe factors.
findings.calculation: L2 settlement authority 50,000 >= total incurred 20,200 (gross settlement 21,000 also within limit). Single payment, no splitting.
findings.explanation: The claim was accepted by an L2 officer, whose settlement authority of 50,000 covers the total incurred of 20,200. It was paid in one payment, with no total loss declaration, exception, litigation or catastrophe uplift involved. No denial occurred, so denial limits do not apply. Authority was held.

findings.rule: Claim must be scored at triage; score 0-29 is Low band and requires normal handling; no mandatory referral triggers apply; unscored claims may not be settled.
findings.explanation: No fraud indicators are recorded, so the sum of triggered points is 0, matching the recorded score of 0. This falls in the Low band (0-29), so normal handling applies, and neither enhanced verification nor SIU referral is required. None of the clause 5.1 triggers are shown on the facts: the claimed value is far below AUD 250,000 and no indicator is triggered. The claim was scored, so settlement was not barred by the scoring obligation.

findings.rule: POL-DOC-005 Appendix A requires POLICE_EVENT (decision stage) for 'collisions under 4.1'. The supplied clauses do not include POL-DOC-005 clause 4.1, so the collisions it covers cannot be determined.
findings.explanation: All other required documents were on file before the decision: CLAIM_FORM, ID_VERIFIED, DRIVER_LICENCE, PHOTOS, TP_DETAILS, LICENCE_VERIFIED, VEHICLE_HISTORY_CHECK, REPAIR_QUOTE_ACCREDITED, ASSESSMENT_REPORT and BANK_VERIFIED. docs_complete_date 2026-05-29 is before the 2026-06-15 decision. The claim is a collision with no police event number on file. Whether POLICE_EVENT is required depends on POL-DOC-005 clause 4.1, which was not supplied. If it applies, accepting without it is a procedural breach, since no waiver is recorded. Not required on the facts: STAT_DEC (22,000 is not above 50,000), PPSR_SEARCH, INDEPENDENT_ASSESSMENT, CTP_REFERENCE (no injury) and GST_DECLARATION (claimant not GST registered). The claim facts do not show the 9.1 checklist, so that was not assessed.

findings.rule: Claimant must receive written acknowledgement within 2 business days of lodgement.
findings.calculation: 5 business days actual - 2 business days allowed = 3 business days late
findings.explanation: Acknowledgement was sent 5 business days after lodgement, exceeding the 2 business day limit. Handler notes say the claim sat in an unassigned queue. No catastrophe event is recorded, so no extension arises.

findings.rule: Claimant must receive a status update at least every 20 business days; a longer gap with no outbound contact is a service breach.

evidence.value: Acknowledgement letter sent 12 May after the claim sat in an unassigned queue. No outbound contact between 12 May and the decision call on 15 June.

findings.calculation: 23 business days gap - 20 business days allowed = 3 business days over
findings.explanation: The longest gap with no outbound contact was 23 business days, which exceeds the 20 business day standard for a non-vulnerable claimant.

findings.rule: Standard claims decided within 20 business days of docs-complete date; overall cap of 4 months; decision communicated within 5 business days; payment within 10 business days of acceptance; triage within 1 business day.
findings.explanation: Decision was 10 business days after docs-complete (limit 20), within the 4-month cap, communicated same day (limit 5), paid 2 business days after acceptance (limit 10), and triaged within 1 business day.

findings.rule: Repair-basis settlement: gross settlement less basic excess; no additional excess for driver aged 25+ with 2+ years full licence; no GST/ITC deduction for non-registered claimant; no total loss below 75% threshold.
findings.calculation: Repair cost 58.3% <= 75%, so repair basis. Additional excess: age 44 (not under 25) and 26 full licence years (not under 2) so 0. Expected excess = 800 + 0 = 800. Net = 21000 - 800 - 0 = 20200, matches net_paid 20200.
findings.explanation: Repair-basis settlement is correct: the vehicle is not a total loss, the excess is the basic AUD 800 with no loading, there is no ITC deduction because the claimant is not GST-registered, and net paid equals gross less excess. No recovery has been recorded, and no clause supplied requires any adjustment to the settlement for it.
